claims.text: Adding a refractory element can improve the strength–plasticity combination of a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Hf or Zr is a suitable refractory-element addition for this intervention.
The proposed benefit should occur after arc melting and drop casting.
The proposed benefit should occur during room-temperature mechanical testing.
Adding the refractory element increases lattice distortion.
Adding the refractory element produces atomic-scale segregation.
Enhanced lattice distortion increases alloy strength.
The modified alloy will have 20% higher yield strength than the reference alloy.
The modified alloy will have 15% higher ductility than the reference alloy.
An alloy without the added refractory element is the appropriate reference.
AlCoCrFeNi is an example of the proposed refractory high-entropy-alloy reference.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis calls for a specific single refractory element, but the intervention leaves the element unresolved between Hf and Zr.
The initial material is specified as a refractory high-entropy alloy, whereas the example reference AlCoCrFeNi does not clearly represent the same refractory-alloy class.

The prediction specifies 20% higher yield strength and 15% higher ductility, but the falsification rule only requires gains of at least 10% and 5%; therefore, outcomes that fail the quantitative prediction can escape falsification.
